title: ISS-2341 architectural recommendation: in-place generalization (option a) for 4-cluster counting-methodology paragraph
short_recommendation: Apply option (a) — in-place generalization of the existing Evaluation Guide methodology paragraph. The hub-and-spoke option (b) modeled on EXP-464 P0's OTS canonical-home pattern does not transfer cleanly here: counting methodology is a single principle stated once in its natural home (Verdict Assignment Criteria), not a critique referenced from many tabs. Option (a) costs ~949 net chars and zero spoke edits; option (b) would cost ~3,000+ chars (hub + 12 spoke cross-links + retained pointer) and N+1 edits per future cluster addition.

inventory.notes_on_inventory: All 16 clustered WINs already carry the detail_group field naming their cluster (verified via wins.json scan). The cluster-membership infrastructure is in place; what is missing is reader-facing prose acknowledging the principle. The methodology paragraph in build-scripts/generate-html.js currently names only the tidal cluster.

sections_json_cluster_mentions.note: Per-section breakdown shows Schumann/cosmological/H(r)/tidal discussions are densely distributed across parts 1, 2, 2b, 4, 6 — meaning per-WIN sections are NOT short stubs that would benefit from offloading methodology to a hub. They already carry their full cluster-root explanations inline. Adding a 'see Counting Methodology' spoke link would add bytes without saving any spoke content.

why_option_a: Option (a) is ~2.4x cheaper in bytes (949 vs ~2,250 net chars).
Option (a) is 13x cheaper in mechanical edits (1 vs 13 site touches).

The detail_group field on each clustered WIN already carries spoke-side cluster membership — adding a parenthetical cross-link to a hub would not reveal new information to the reader that detail_group does not already.

The natural reading path is: reader sees verdict tally → reader asks 'how are these counted?' → reader navigates to Evaluation Guide → Verdict Assignment Criteria. The current methodology paragraph is already at the end of that path. Generalizing it in place is what the reader's reading path expects.

EXP-464 P0's OTS canonical-home pattern does not transfer. OTS is a single self-contained critique that should be findable from many tabs (Overview, Self-Contradictions §1.4, Part 6) because the critique is the primary takeaway of any of those tabs. Counting methodology is not a primary takeaway — it is a transparency caveat that lives where the verdict assignment criteria live.

Option (a)'s maintainability is strictly better for future cluster additions. A 5th cluster appearing in a future review (e.g., a hypothetical refraction-coupling cluster) would be one paragraph edit in option (a), vs one hub edit plus N spoke edits in option (b).
decision_rationale.counter_argument_considered: Option (b) would give per-WIN readers an explicit click-back-to-methodology path that option (a) lacks. However, this is only valuable if the reader of a per-WIN section needs to be reminded that cluster membership exists. The detail_group field already surfaces in the per-WIN render and names the cluster. A reader who notices 'detail_group: WIN-002/029/038/061' has the cluster information. A reader who does not notice that field is unlikely to follow a parenthetical link either. The marginal navigation value of option (b) is low.
decision_rationale.decision: Recommend option (a). Apply the in-place generalization patch below.

We assign the same verdict structure to each WIN that the dome claims: if the dome counts five tidal constituents (M2, S2, K1, O1, N2) as five separate predictions, we evaluate each as a separate claim. Five tidal WINs (045, 046, 049, 050, 051) each receive Self-Contradicted because the dome's local moon geometry fails independently for each constituent's period. We acknowledge that all five derive from one underlying geometric impossibility — a 2,534 km moon cannot produce semidiurnal tides regardless of constituent. We apply this transparency standard symmetrically: when we note that the dome inflates its count by splitting one observation into multiple claims, the reader should know that our verdict count reflects the same granularity.

kernel_of_truth: The operator's intuition that 'the 4 clusters' counting methodology likely has substantial overlap' is correct: all 4 clusters DO share the same transparency principle, and all 4 cluster-root explanations DO involve similar prose structure (name the cluster, name the WINs, name the shared geometric root). The hub-and-spoke architectural treatment IS the right pattern for content that is referenced from many tabs (cf. EXP-464 P0 OTS). The reason it does not apply here is not that the operator's pattern recognition is wrong — it is that this particular content already has its 'canonical home' in the Verdict Assignment Criteria subsection, and the spokes already carry the cluster-root content in per-WIN detail rather than being short stubs that would benefit from offloading. The architectural treatment is the right one; the file structure already implements it implicitly.
why_it_doesnt_save_the_argument: Not applicable — this is an architectural-recommendation EXP, not a verdict-defense EXP.

anticipated_objections.objection: Curmudgeon may push back that option (a) keeps the methodology paragraph hidden inside Evaluation Guide where casual readers may never look. A canonical hub linked from each per-WIN section would surface the methodology to a wider audience.
anticipated_objections.response: The methodology paragraph is a transparency caveat, not a primary takeaway. Its placement in Verdict Assignment Criteria is intentional — readers asking 'how are wins counted?' find it; readers who do not ask that question are not the target audience for it. A per-WIN spoke link to a hub increases the link clutter in already-dense per-WIN sections without adding information the detail_group field does not already convey.

anticipated_objections.objection: Curmudgeon may push back that the existing EXP-452 P1 replace text was already option (a), and this EXP is redundant.
anticipated_objections.response: EXP-452 P1 was authored as a mechanical generalization without explicit comparison against the hub-and-spoke alternative the operator raised. The operator's HNOTE explicitly commissioned an analyst evaluation of the architectural question. This EXP delivers that evaluation, validates the existing P1 direction, and refines the patch text with explicit numerical anchors. Treating it as redundant would discard the architectural reasoning the operator asked for.

anticipated_objections.objection: A future curmudgeon could note that 'natural home' is a soft argument and the OTS precedent could in principle apply to any content.
anticipated_objections.response: Concrete distinguishing feature: OTS is referenced from Overview, Self-Contradictions §1.4, and Part 6 — three tabs whose primary topics differ. Counting methodology is referenced from one tab (Evaluation Guide). One-tab content does not need a hub; multi-tab content does.

summary_for_decider: Recommend option (a) in-place generalization for ISS-2341. Apply patch EXP-626-P1 (supersedes EXP-452-P1). ISS-2342 separately scoped to analyst-baby per HNOTE's class hint. HNOTE-OPERATOR-ISS-2341-2342-REWRITE-COMMISSION-001 should be marked consumed-pending-verification with verification_artifact_path pointing at this EXP file; full consumption flips when baby's ISS-2342 EXP lands.
